facets.detail: BUG live in 2.2.0 (fix open in PR #80): presence check is substring includes(), so a CLAUDE.md that merely MENTIONS @coldstart.md in backticked prose (coldstart's own repo does) makes init report 'already imports' and skip writing the real import line — and Claude Code does not resolve imports inside code spans, so the guidance never loads. Fix = standalone-line check, symmetric with unwire's line-based strip.

Writes .coldstart/.coldstartignore (comments-only template; defaults live in hooks/ignore.mjs) and ensures a sibling .coldstart/.gitignore carries the .coldstartignore line so the file stays personal even in shared-notebook repos.

bakes ONLY the absolute install path (resolveHooksDir) into the capture command - never a repo path. The hook defaults --root to cwd, so one identical invocation works for every host and every repo, and npm updates are picked up automatically.

writes .claude/commands/capture-notes.md. Uses Claude's leading-! expansion so the checklist is injected into the prompt at submit time rather than the agent having to run it. Fully-owned file, overwritten every init.
writes .cursor/commands/capture-notes.md as a PLAIN prompt template - Cursor commands have no ! expansion, so the body must ask the agent to run the command itself.

writes .agents/skills/capture-notes/SKILL.md, NOT a Codex prompt: Codex custom prompts live in global ~/.codex/prompts and are deprecated, so they cannot carry repo-scoped wiring. Skills are repo-scoped (walked up to the repo root) and REQUIRE name + description frontmatter.

summary: Generates the agent guidance and wires the chosen client (Claude/Cursor/Codex/other), then sets up the notebook; also exports the idempotency detectors that unwire reuses so removal stays symmetric with how init writes. CHANGED 2026-07-24: init now BLOCKS on the first index instead of exiting immediately. ensureKeeper only spawns the detached keeper and returns, so init used to finish mid-walk and the agent's very first find hit a cache miss, printed the 'keeper is still building this repo' message from src/cli.ts, and fell back to grep — a real user read that as coldstart being broken. It now awaits waitForKeeperCache (180s, progress callback) and prints a distinct line for each of the three outcomes, so a spawn failure or a slow repo still leaves a correctly wired repo whose first query builds lazily.

summary: Generates coldstart.md and wires each host (Claude/Cursor/Codex/Other), exporting the idempotency detectors unwire reuses so removal is symmetric with how init writes. 2026-08-01: the three per-host user-command writers were generalised. USER_COMMANDS is a table of {name, invocation, description, skillDescription, instructions} and wireClaudeCommand / wireCursorCommand / wireCodexSkill take an entry, so adding a command means one table row reaching all three hosts — a host silently getting one command and not the other was the failure mode this removes. New REPAIR_COMMAND ('repair-notes') alongside CAPTURE_COMMAND; unlike capture (which runs a hook in --manual mode) it invokes the CLI directly, `node <install>/dist/index.js kb repair --root .`, because repair reads only the notebook — no session, no index. Per-host differences are unchanged and load-bearing: Claude `!`-expands so output lands in the prompt, Cursor has no `!` expansion, Codex needs name/description frontmatter in .agents/skills. wireClaudeCaptureCommand/wireCursorCaptureCommand/wireCodexCaptureSkill remain as thin back-compat wrappers.

USER_COMMANDS.repair.instructions is DELIBERATELY thin — it says only 'follow the instructions it prints' and never restates how to fix a note, because repairWorklist already carries those instructions and a second copy in each host wrapper is three more places to drift; tests/init.test.ts asserts NEGATIVELY that no host body contains 'kb write', so helpfully expanding this string breaks a test on purpose. wireClaudeCaptureCommand/wireCursorCaptureCommand/wireCodexCaptureSkill remain as thin back-compat wrappers.

summary: init.ts owns coldstart init/setup for all three hosts. USER_COMMANDS is the single source of truth for every user-invoked slash-command/skill (capture-notes, repair-notes, repair-aliases): one row (invocation/description/skillDescription/instructions) per command, rendered by wireClaudeCommand/wireCursorCommand/wireCodexSkill into each host's own format — adding a command means adding one row, not editing three hosts by hand. Deliberately thin `instructions`: the actual guidance lives in the command's own worklist output (repairWorklist / aliasRepairWorklist), never restated here, so CLI/MCP/hosts cannot drift apart. init's main flow also calls mechanicalSymbolRepair once on the upgrade path.
